$Comment: Anvil work station: two fully self-contained actions, Convert (sharpen a vanilla metal bar) and Enhance (a Stamp-step ritual that rolls stats onto a placed weapon), each read top to bottom with nothing inherited from the station or from each other. The station's only shared groups are Identity (name/desc) and the ordered Actions array itself: everything about how a job runs, including the hammer gate, lives inside that job's own action now, so Tool, Worker (Hold plus Camera plus Animation plus Puppet), and Moments.Completion are authored IDENTICALLY on both Convert and Enhance rather than once at the station level. Both actions therefore repeat the same Tool.Ids hammer gate (Tool_Hammer_Crude, Tool_Hammer_Iron; no Tags.Family:["Hammer"] exists on the real vanilla hammer items, so this is the fallback Ids route), the same Worker.Hold (the proven movement-lock effect, not a mount), the same Worker.Camera.Recipe LookRot fixed look, the same Worker.Puppet (mount the player, hide their body, spawn a skinned double performing the work), and the same Moments.Completion (a legendary-chest-open cue), verbatim on both. Own-asset references and step ids are authored PascalCase to match the file or key they name; matching stays case-insensitive so a casing slip never breaks content. Reuses the vanilla Anvil bench model (Common/Blocks/Benches/Anvil.blockymodel), no new art. Select is the diegetic action-selection matcher: Convert selects on any held vanilla bar in the Metal_Bars family, Enhance on any held weapon-shaped item (Function: Weapon). Custody's own Input leaf is the separate PLACEMENT-acceptance matcher and stays distinct from Select: Convert derives its acceptance from Recipe.Conversions with no explicit Custody.Input, Enhance authors one explicitly since it has no conversions to derive from. Recipe is now a single group per action rather than a list, one recipe per action, so Convert authors Recipe.Conversions directly (ten metal-bar sharpenings, each an Ingredient array on both sides, the native CraftingRecipe shape) with no separate per-recipe Tool override; the action's own Tool is the only gate now. Enhance ritual steps use the orthogonal-phase step model: Strike1/Strike2/Settle are pure Duration beats (650/650/900ms) carrying their own Puppet.Clip/Presentation. The Stamp step keeps its Stamp phase group (Reagents is the shared Ingredient leaf: ResourceTypeId+Quantity) and holds an extra 800ms after the stamp commits so the empty-hands flourish reads as a deliberate pause before session completion (Puppet.Prop.Source None already shows empty hands; the added Duration makes the hold real). Caps live on the Budgets[] array: a flat {Points:30} entry plus a scaled {PointsPer:0.5, Factors:[{Factor:stat, Param:MMO_Level_SMITHING}]} entry, composed via the MIN rule (StampCapEngine) so the effective total budget is the flat-plus-scaled pairing in every case. PerStat is unchanged. Custody/display knobs (Convert.Custody.Display, Enhance.Custody.Display incl. the facing-relative Offset/Rotation weapon pose) carry over unchanged from the prior authoring, unaffected by the action-first regrouping. Enhance's weapon pose derives from Weapon_Sword_Crude's actual blockymodel axes rather than a guess: the item references a real Model (Items/Weapons/Sword/Crude.blockymodel), so the ItemComponent prop renders that 3D mesh, not an icon-extruded flat billboard. Model axes (root frame, at identity): all visible geometry sits under the model's Handle node, whose orientation quaternion (-0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5) maps Handle-local +X (the pommel-to-tip long axis) to model +Y, local +Y (blade width) to model -Z, and local +Z (blade thickness, the flat-face normal) to model -X. At identity the blade length runs along model +Y (up), the flat-normal is model +/-X (broad faces point sideways), and the cutting edges point along model +/-Z. Engine composition: RpgStations resolveRotationRadians builds a Rotation3f from the Rotation group's Pitch/Yaw/Roll degrees; getQuaternion uses JOML rotationYXZ(yaw, pitch, roll) = Ry(yaw)*Rx(pitch)*Rz(roll), so Roll applies first in model space, then Pitch, then Yaw; the placed block's facing yaw adds into Yaw (facing-relative). Target pose: blade lying flat, broad face up, edge sideways, hilt flat. With Pitch 0, Rotation {Yaw:90, Roll:90} maps model +X (flat normal) to world +Y (up), model +Y (length) to world +Z (block front), model +Z (edge) to world +X (block right), which is the target. In-game validation confirmed the flat-up twist but with the blade lying across the anvil rather than along it; the authored pose is {Yaw:0, Roll:90}: the 90-degree roll maps flat-normal +X to up, length +Y to world -X (along the anvil's long axis), edge +Z to +Z. The hilt sits toward block right (+X, the pommel-anchored render origin); to swap hilt/tip ends, author Rotation.Yaw:180 and flip Offset.X's sign. Cross-checked against two other observed poses: {Pitch:90} alone maps length +Y to world +Z (horizontal, correct) but edge +Z to world -Y (vertical, edge-up); {Pitch:90,Roll:90} maps length +Y to world -X (a 90-degree spin in the horizontal plane vs {Pitch:90}) with the edge still vertical. {Pitch:90,Roll:90} fails because Roll applies before Pitch, so it spins the still-upright blade in-plane instead of twisting it about its own long axis; twisting via Yaw (applied last) is the fix, so {Yaw:90, Roll:90} with no Pitch lays it flat. In this derived frame, Roll is the flat-vs-edge twist knob (Roll:90 = flat up, Roll:270/-90 = flat down but still lying flat, Roll:0/180 = blade stands vertical), and Yaw is the horizontal-direction knob. Offset: the render origin sits near the pommel, so the mesh extends most of its length toward the tip (world +Z / block front) and overhangs that edge; Offset.X:0.4 pulls the weapon back toward the anvil-top center along its own length. Offset.Y:0.55 accounts for the flat pose sitting vertically thinner than an on-edge pose at the same offset. In-game tuning ladder for this derived frame (plain JSON leaves, no engine rebuild): (1) blade spun the wrong way in the horizontal plane, adjust Rotation.Yaw by +/-90; (2) blade on its edge instead of flat, confirm no Pitch leaf is present and keep Roll:90, if flat but the wrong broad face is up, flip the twist sign Roll:90 to Roll:270; (3) blade standing vertical, Roll drifted to 0/180, set back to Roll:90; (4) sunk into or floating above the anvil, Offset.Y in 0.05 steps; (5) overhangs one end along the blade length, Offset.X in 0.1 steps (smaller values slide toward the tip end, larger toward the hilt end); (6) off-center sideways, Offset.Z in 0.1 steps; (7) hilt on the wrong end, Rotation.Yaw 0 to 180 and flip Offset.X's sign. Fallback if the client's item-mesh renderer ignores pitch/yaw/roll for a bare ItemComponent prop: remove the Rotation leaves (the weapon stays upright, zero regression), keep the schema, and escalate to a lying-flat custom display block or a dedicated prop model. Facing-relative context: Custody.Display Offset/Rotation are relative to the placed block's own yaw; RpgStations reads the block's rotation index at spawn, rotates the horizontal Offset (X/Z) by it, and folds the yaw into Rotation.Yaw. Authored +Z = block front, +X = block right, Y vertical; a default-orientation placement (yaw 0) is the identity so the block frame equals the world frame. Convert.Custody.Display (placed ingot, Offset.Y 0.52) and the sawmill's placed log (Offset.Y -0.1) author only a vertical Offset.Y with no horizontal shift and no Rotation, so both stay byte-identical at any orientation. Step-synced puppet swings: the Enhance ritual's Strike1/Strike2 steps author a per-step Puppet.Clip of MMO_Emote_Hammer so the skinned puppet visibly hammers on both strike beats, played once at each step's iteration entry; the generic engage/swing puppet clip is suppressed for the whole ritual so there is no double-fire. Settle authors no clip (the puppet idles for the settling pause), and Stamp keeps its Puppet.Prop.Source None empty-hands override (a Prop but no Clip, so no hammer swing fires on the stamp beat).
